Accused is before this under Section 482 of Cr.P.C with a prayer to quash the entire proceedings against him in Crime No.131/2021 registered by Sindhanoor Town Police Station, Raichur for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 408 and 420 of IPC on the basis of the first information dated 30.11.2021 received from Yenkob D/o Shivanna, Manager of the Karnataka State Cooperative Marketing Federation Limited, Sindhanoor pending on the file of the Prl. Civil Judge and JMFC,
Sindhanoor.

2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
3.

The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that in respect of the alleged misappropriation for the period from 14.06.2016 to 30.09.2019 the first NC: 2024:KHC-K:4898 information is submitted belatedly on 30.11.2021 which has resulted in registration of FIR in Crime No.131/2021.
He submits that till date there is no progress in the investigation and no charge-sheet is filed against the petitioner.

Petitioner was earlier working as Manager of the very same Federation and for extraneous reasons the present Manager of the Federation has lodged a false complaint against petitioner alleging misappropriation which is not supported by any documents.
He submits that the audit report of the Federation for the period from 2016 to 2019 do not reflect the alleged misappropriation.
Petitioner who had retired in the month of June, 2017 had continued in service at the request of the management for a further period till 30.09.2019.
Thereafter, the impugned criminal proceeding is initiated against the petitioner in the year 2021.

Accordingly, he prays to Somashekharappa vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192635167/
2 allow the petition.
4.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1/State and learned counsel for respondent No.2 who has filed application for vacating NC: 2024:KHC-K:4898 interim order granted by this Court have opposed the petition.

5. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that the petitioner had given an undertaking in the form of affidavit to the management of the Federation on 27.11.2018 admitting that he had supplied the fertilizer stock to various primary societies and private dealers without instruction from the Federation.
He submits that in the audit for the period from April, 2020 to September, 2020 the alleged misappropriation by the petitioner finds a place.
Investigation in the case is under progress.
All the aforesaid materials are placed before the Investigating Officer and accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

He has placed reliance on the judgment of hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kishan Singh (Dead) Through Lrs. V/s Gurpal Singh And Others reported in (2010) 8 SCC 775.
6.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
A perusal of the averments made in the first information dated 16.11.2021 submitted by the Manager NC: 2024:KHC-K:4898 of the Federation to the Station House Officer of Sindhanur Police,
which has resulted in registration of FIR in Crime No.131/2021 for the aforesaid offences against the petitioner would go to show that allegation of misappropriation of amount of Rs.8,06,05,863.42 against the petitioner is for the period from 14.06.2016 to 30.09.2019.
The petitioner was earlier serving as the branch manager of the Federation and he had retired from service on 30.06.2017.
Thereafter, at the request of the Federation on contract basis, service of the petitioner was continued till 03.08.2019.
Subsequently, for administrative reasons petitioner's service was continued for a further period of 2 months from 01.08.2019 to 30.09.2019 and thereafter, he was relived from duty.

7. Allegation against the petitioner is that for the period from 14.06.2016 to 30.09.2019, he had supplied fertilizers from the federation to other primary cooperative societies and private dealers,
without due permission of the federation, which had caused loss to the federation.

NC: 2024:KHC-K:4898 It is alleged in the first information that the petitioner had not collected any advance amount prior to supply of the fertilizers to primary cooperative societies and private dealers and he also had failed to recover the amount from the primary cooperative societies and private dealers, to which he had supplied fertilizers, allegedly without permission of the federation.

The said allegations are not sufficient to arrive at the conclusion that the petitioner has misappropriated the amount of the Federation, since there is no such allegation in the first information that the petitioner had collected any amount from the primary cooperative societies and private dealers and thereafter, misappropriated the same.

8. In the affidavit of undertaking dated 27.11.2018, allegedly furnished by the petitioner to the management, which is produced along with the application for vacating the stay filed by respondent No.2, the following averments are found in para 3 and 4 of the said affidavit.

sentences.text: 3. I submit that, while I am working as Manager in Sindhanur Branch of Federation on my own I have supplied fertilizer stocks to various primary societies and private dealers to an extent of 1867.900 ton, amounting to Rs.3,56,78,250.00 without instructions and authorization of the Federation.

4. I submit that, the aforesaid supply of fertilizer stock was made on my own risk, hence, I hereby undertakes to recover the due amounting to sum of Rs.3,56,78,250.00 from primary societies and private dealers and to remit the same to the Federation account on or before 10.01.2019, failing which I hereby states that, the Federation is at liberty to recover the aforesaid amount together with interest and cost from me out of my salary and by way of attachment of movable and immovable properties belonging to me.
The Federation is also at liberty to take any kind of recovery steps against me in case of my default to recover and deposit the aforesaid amount within the time agreed upon."

9. Even in the affidavit, it is nowhere stated that the petitioner had recovered or collected any money in respect of the fertilizers supplied to the primary cooperative societies and private dealers and had misappropriated or misused the said amount.
It is not in dispute that in the audit report for the period from 2016 to 2019, the alleged misappropriation by the petitioner was not found out.

It is for the first time in the audit report for the period of April 2020 to September 2020, an averment NC:
2024:KHC-K:4898 is found with regard to the supply of fertilizers by the petitioners, total amount of which is Rs.8,06,05,863.42.
Even in the said audit report, there is no such averment that the said amount has been misappropriated by the petitioner.

Only allegation found in the audit report is that the petitioner had supplied the fertilizers to primary cooperative societies and private dealers without obtaining permission from the Federation and he had neither collected money from primary cooperative societies and private dealers nor had he recovered the amount in respect of the fertilizer supplied by him.
10. Learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has submitted that the recovery proceedings has already been initiated against the petitioner for recovery of aforesaid amount.

Merely for the reason that recovery proceedings has been initiated against the petitioner, the impugned criminal proceedings cannot be permitted to continue against the petitioner, unless respondent No.2 is able to prima facie show that the petitioner has misappropriated NC: 2024:KHC-K:4898 the aforesaid amount and there is some documentary evidence in support of the said allegation.
Neither the first information nor the audit report states that the petitioner has misappropriated the aforesaid amount.

Only allegation against the petitioner is that he had supplied the fertilizers to primary cooperative societies and private dealers without permission of the Federation and he thereafter failed to recover the amount towards the supply of fertilizers made by him.

Since, the impugned criminal proceedings is initiated without there being prima facie material to prove the allegations made against the petitioner, the continuation of the impugned criminal proceedings would amount to abuse of process of law.

11. In the case of P.Swaroopa Rani V/s M.Hari Narayana Alias Hari Babu reported in (2008) 5 SCC 765 the hon'ble Supreme Court in Para 11 has observed as follows:

12. The same principle has been reiterated in the case of Kishan Singh (Supra).

Para 15 of the aforesaid judgment reads as follows:
"15. In P.Swaroopa Rani v. M. Hari Narayana this Court has held as under (SCC pp.769-71, paras 11, 13 & 18)
11.

entities.text: P.Swaroopa Rani v. M. Hari Narayana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is, however, well settled that in a given case, civil proceedings and criminal proceedings can proceed simultaneously.
Whether civil proceedings or criminal proceedings shall be stayed depends upon the facts and circumstances of each case.
13. Filing of an independent criminal proceedings, although initiated in terms of some observations made by the civil Court, is not barred under any statute.
18. It goes without saying that the respondent shall be at liberty to take recourse to such a remedy which is available to him in law.
We have interfered with the impugned order only because in law simultaneous proceedings of a civil and a criminal case are permissible."
In the present case, the material available on record would go to show that in respect of the allegations made against the petitioner, there is absolutely no material.
The allegation against the petitioner is required to be primarily proved by documentary evidence and in the absence of the same, the impugned criminal proceedings cannot be permitted to be continued.
It is trite that the judgments can be relied as precedents, only if the same are applicable to the facts and circumstances of the case.

The judgment on which the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has placed reliance,
cannot be made applicable to the facts and circumstances of the present case.

14. Under these circumstances, I am of the considered opinion that the continuation of the impugned criminal proceedings against the petitioner would not only amount to abuse of process of law, but the same will also cause untold hardship and embarrassment to the petitioner.

Accordingly,
